entityDescription:
Domel, d.o.o. is a global development supplier of electric motors, vacuum motors, blowers and components. Our long tradition and the loyalty of our employees are the foundation of our success.
Domel’s solutions are sustainable and innovative. Our dedication to innovation has positioned us as leaders in several key technology areas such as universal vacuum motors, brushless DC blowers, and brushless DC motors, including the most efficient permanent magnet synchronous motors. Domel is a development leader in the vacuum motor market. We create motors for household and industrial appliances, such as floor care machines, gardening equipment and power tools, as well as for HVAC, healthcare and medicine, the alternative energy sector and automotive industry.
Our business processes employ high levels of technology, automation and robotisation, which form a basis for building competitiveness and excellence. Vertical integration has brought us broad technological knowledge, all the way from the initial concept to the final product. Components are manufactured from laminates, aluminium, thermoplastics and BMC thermosetting parts, with the support of our own tool shop.
The quality of our finished products is reflected in their exceptionally long lifetimes, very low noise level and proven ultra-high efficiency, which reduces electricity consumption for the end user. In this way, we contribute to sustainable economic growth and a green future.
Our motors power over 300 million appliances in premium and consumer markets worldwide. We build long-term partnerships with our customers.
The company, headquartered in Slovenia, was founded in 1946. We supply our products to all continents.

entityName: Oficina Técnica de Estudios y Control de Obras, S.A.
entityDescription:
OFICINA TÉCNICA DE ESTUDIOS Y CONTROL DE OBRAS, S.A. (OFITECO) is a Spanish engineering company founded in 1971. With the always growing concerns about dam and reservoir safety, combined with the fundamental role played by transportation in the field of environmental engineering, OFITECO has highly developed in two main fields of activities: hydraulic and transport infrastructures.
The first sector includes dams and reservoirs, flood management, hydropower, water supply, wastewater treatment plants, irrigation, or river restoration. On the other hand, among the topic treated within the second sector, there are roads, highways, railways, and high-speed and underground lines. Tunnels, viaducts, and hillsides are also widely treated by the company.
OFITECO oversees all the services related to the life phases of both hydraulic and transportation infrastructures, from the design and the construction to the entire operational functioning.‎ 
During the construction phase, OFITECO manages the monitoring and quality control activities throughout the entire duration of the works. Besides, a particular focus is given to the monitoring, surveillance, and automation of dams, tunnels, and bridges.
Similarly, during the operation phase, flood risk management techniques are applied to dams, hydrometeorological networks, and canals. Detailed inspections and corrective actions are carried out for dams, tunnels, and viaducts.
OFITECO has constantly focused on R&D. The contribution of the company to the research and development fields is based on the applications of DamData, TunnelData, and BridgeData, which have been proven to be excellent real-time web services for remote data management in dam monitoring.
OFITECO is a fully established company in the SPANISH MARKET, holding offices in numerous Spanish cities such as Madrid, Valencia, Zaragoza, Granada, and Valladolid. Moreover, it is also consolidated on a more international perspective, conducting projects in Canada, Peru, Colombia, Guatemala, Algeria, Iraq, Qatar, Panama, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Georgia, ‎ Poland, and Saudi Arabia. OFITECO holds a branch office in Peru.

entityName: AECSIC - CENTRO NACIONAL INSTITUTO ESPAÑOL DE OCEANOGRAFÍA
entityDescription:
The Spanish Institute of Oceanography was created by Royal Decree of April 17, 1914, is a public research organization (OPI) dedicated to research in marine science, especially in relation to scientific knowledge of the oceans, sustainability of fishing resources and the marine environment. The IEO depends on the Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities.The IEO is not limited to carrying out basic and applied research, it also provides scientific and technological advice to administrations in matters related to oceanography and marine sciences. In fact, according to the Marine Fisheries Act of 2001, the IEO is the investigative and advisory body for the fisheries sector policy of the Government. In addition, it is the scientific and technological representative of Spain in most of the forums and international organizations related to the sea and its resources.
The IEO is an autonomous body, with its own legal personality and assets, with an approximate workforce of 700 people -of which 80% is research staff and research support-.
The budget of the IEO exceeds 65 million euros and has a wide geographical coverage and important facilities. It has a central office in Madrid and nine coastal oceanographic centers: A Coruña, Baleares (Palma de Mallorca), Cádiz, Canary Islands (Santa Cruz de Tenerife), Gijón, Málaga (Fuengirola), Murcia (San Pedro del Pinatar), Santander and Vigo five plants of experimentation of marine cultures; twelve gauge stations and one satellite image receiving station. Its oceanographic fleet, with more than twenty vessels, has five important oceanographic vessels, among which the 46 m twin vessels stand out. Ramón Margalef and Ángeles Alvariño.
The Spanish Institute of Oceanography performs basic and applied research in oceanography and marine sciences, as well as other services for scientific-technological development and maintenance of industrial, social and business activities, with the aim of increasing scientific knowledge of the oceans and that they make a sustainable use of them.
Its basic functions are:
- Scientific research in oceanography and marine sciences and multidisciplinary study of the sea.
- Advice to the General State Administration on its fishing and marine policy in general.
- Representation of Spain in international fisheries and marine science organizations.
- Promotion of cooperation in marine research at the regional, national and international levels.
- Train marine researchers and disseminate oceanographic knowledge.
A brief summary of the activities of the IEO includes: conducting quality research in oceanography and marine science; represent Spain in international forums related to oceanography and fisheries; study vulnerable marine ecosystems; develop, coordinate, carry out and manage research programs on fisheries resources as well as on marine crops; report on scientific and technological projects that are submitted for consultation and that are related to the marine sciences; study the seas and continental margins with a multidisciplinary approach; establish and participate in agreements with public and private organizations, both national and international, to carry out research projects and other scientific and technological activities; participate in international scientific research programs.

Asociacija DRONEA (www.dronea.lt), a non-profit organization, is a partnership of the leading stakeholders interested in innovative drone solutions, research and development, and performance and political processes to advance a drone ecosystem. 
Together with its partners and affiliates, DRONEA represents experts from across the aviation community, from civil air navigation service providers to civil airspace users, academia, and municipalities. The members of the Association at all levels demonstrate the corresponding qualities of commitment, flexibility, innovation, and team-working. 
It is worth mentioning that DRONEA's key members were actively involved in the successful implementation of the Baltic Functional Airspace Block, and the development of the interoperable iTEC, a next-generation air traffic management system concept as well as in SESAR activities. 
As an Association we provide the framework for academia and industry, thought leaders and technology experts, regulatory and advisory bodies to connect, collaborate and promote the development of a drone ecosystem that is simple to use, affordable, commercially and operationally friendly, yet capable of addressing all societal concerns such as safety, security, privacy, and environmental protection.
DRONEA is an “outward-facing” organisation, effectively interacting with a wide range of stakeholders, formal and informal, working in an integrated way within the Association, and has close links to their expert counterparts in other EU or multinational structures.

JEDA aims to develop and maintain a common understanding of the seamless integration of UAS/RPAS into aviation and the European airspace system.
